newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST-Polish '96 GDP seen rising 6.3-6.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Polish '96 GDP seen rising 6.3-6.6 pct.

text.p: Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) growth is likely to fall to between 6.3 and 6.6 percent in 1996 from last year's seven percent but will exceed the 5.5 percent government forecast, a study predicted on Tuesday.

But the study, by an institute of the Central Statistics Office (GUS) and the Polish Academy of Sciences (PAN), said GDP growth was kept high by soaring domestic demand for investment and consumer goods.
It said the gap between the 9-10 percent growth in domestic demand and the overall rate of GDP growth indicated the economy might be overheating.
"In our view the economy is in the phase of being overheated and it may be necessary to 'cool down' the final demand in 1997," the report said.

The report's concern was shared by central bank head Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz, who told Nowa Europa economic daily that the bank might raise interest rates slightly to keep the recently soaring credit growth in check.
GUS-PAN said it projected a 10 percent rise in individual consumption in 1996 and a 22 percent rise in investment.

"On the one hand high investment and consumer demand resulted in moving production from exports to the domestic market and on the other it has brought a strong impulse stimulating imports and led to worsening of the foreign trade balance," it said.

The institute, which in mid-year predicted GDP growth of 4.8 percent, said it had revised its forecast mainly because of high household demand but also because of higher than expected agriculural production.
